<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The CPU monitor tests exercise generic threading, psutil CPU-time accounting, and Prometheus metrics. They do not require Xeon-specific hardware.

An existing test-isolation race caused the Xeon PR job to fail: the real monitor thread from the first test remains alive and can call the second test's mocked `time.sleep` with `0.1`, while the assertion expects `3.0`. Failure evidence: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39217692176/job/117945459734.

The crash-dump integration test also exercises generic diagnostics rather than Xeon-specific behavior. Its intentional server crash successfully writes the dump, but the fixture fail-fast watcher treats the expected server exit as a failure and aborts the test process with exit code 137. Failure evidence: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39191014606/job/117863701840.

This PR removes both tests from Xeon per-commit CI. CPU monitor coverage remains in generic CPU nightly; crash-dump coverage remains in CUDA and AMD nightly, with no CPU registration retained for that test. The existing thread-isolation and fail-fast issues are not fixed here.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Delete `register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="stage-b-test-cpu-intel")` from `test/registered/unit/observability/test_cpu_monitor.py`.
- Preserve `register_cpu_ci(est_time=60, suite="base-a-test-cpu", nightly=True)` unchanged.
- Delete `register_cpu_ci(est_time=48, suite="stage-b-test-cpu-intel")` and its now-unused import from `test/registered/debug_utils/test_crash_dump.py`.
- Preserve the crash-dump test's CUDA and AMD nightly registrations unchanged.
- No test logic, production code, or workflow changes.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

No model-output changes. Validation:

- `python3 scripts/lint/check_registered_tests.py test/registered/unit/observability/test_cpu_monitor.py test/registered/debug_utils/test_crash_dump.py` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed before committing.
- Commit-time pre-commit hooks - passed, including Python AST, isort, Ruff, and registered-test validation.
- Exact registration check below - passed for both files; confirms that the original nightly registrations remain and neither test retains a Xeon registration:

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import runpy

ci = runpy.run_path('python/sglang/test/ci/ci_register.py')
HW = ci['HWBackend']
expected = {
    'test/registered/unit/observability/test_cpu_monitor.py': [(HW.CPU, 'base-a-test-cpu', True, 60.0, None)],
    'test/registered/debug_utils/test_crash_dump.py': [(HW.CUDA, 'nightly-test-1-gpu-large', False, 70.0, None), (HW.AMD, 'nightly-amd-1-gpu', True, 40.0, None)],
}
for path, want in expected.items():
    registries, has_main_entry = ci['ut_parse_one_file'](path)
    assert has_main_entry, path
    got = [(r.backend, r.effective_suite, r.nightly, r.est_time, r.disabled) for r in registries]
    assert got == want, (path, got)
    print(f'PASS: {path}: original nightly registrations retained; no Xeon registration')
PY
```

Runtime tests were not run: this changes CI registration only and deliberately leaves the existing flaky test logic untouched. The registry parser was loaded directly to avoid unrelated runtime dependencies (a normal package import requires `orjson`, unavailable in the current Python environment).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

Not run: no inference code or performance behavior changes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Unchecked items are not applicable to this registration-only removal; existing tests and nightly coverage are retained.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
